usageNotes: Use this to discover which mediated device (mdev) types a PCI device supports before assigning one to a VM — required for GPU partitioning workflows (e.g. NVIDIA vGPU, Intel GVT-g). The node must be online and the host kernel/driver must already expose mdev types via sysfs; if no mdev types are registered the response will be an empty array. Requires Sys.Audit or Sys.Modify at the root level.

examples.summary: List mdev types for an NVIDIA GPU at PCI address 0000:01:00.0 on node pve1

tips: The 'available' field in each returned item shows remaining free instances — a value of 0 means every slot of that mdev type is already allocated to a VM.
You can pass either a raw PCI address (e.g. 0000:01:00.0) or a Proxmox PCI mapping name (e.g. gpu-nvidia) as pci-id-or-mapping.
If the driver does not register mdev support in sysfs, this endpoint returns an empty array rather than an error — verify the correct vGPU driver is installed and loaded on the node.
Use get_nodes_node_hardware_pci to enumerate available PCI devices on the node before calling this endpoint.
